summary: Pinned the SkiaSharp renderer stack, embedded the bundled font, wired the font identity into the render fingerprint, and shipped the license notices. src/ArrTags/ArrTags.csproj now references SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux 3.119.4 (the Jellyfin 12.0.0 host version, no HarfBuzzSharp before the task 4.8 spike), and both packages.lock.json files were regenerated so locked-mode restore stays valid. DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf (708,920 bytes, SHA-256 5c1247acef7f2b8522a31742c76d6adcb5569bacc0be7ceaa4dc39dd252ce895, name-table version 2.37) was copied into the repository and embedded as the stable logical resource ArrTags.Resources.DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf. The new RenderFontIdentity type records family/style/version/exact byte length/SHA-256/resource logical name, exposes a read-only stream over the exact embedded bytes, and RenderOutputPolicy.Default.FontIdentity is that identity; RenderFingerprint records the full identity descriptor so any changed font field changes the output fingerprint. licenses/DejaVu-Fonts-License.txt, licenses/SkiaSharp-LICENSE.txt, licenses/SkiaSharp-THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md were added, and the PackagePlugin target copies the notices and license files into the plugin package. BundledFontTests adds 12 cases proving the resource name, readability, non-empty exact length, and SHA-256, and that the default output policy consumes the identity; RenderFingerprintTests gains a font-SHA-256 sensitivity case (13 new tests total). Build and test pass with 0 warnings and 438 passing tests.

Confirmed the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 managed, SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux 3.119.4, SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Win32 3.119.4, and SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.macOS 3.119.4 packages are present in the local NuGet cache (the exact version pinned by the Jellyfin 12.0.0 host).

Verified the provided font source: sha256sum = 5c1247acef7f2b8522a31742c76d6adcb5569bacc0be7ceaa4dc39dd252ce895, stat size = 708920, and the TTF name table reports 'Version 2.37' (grep -aP on the UTF-16BE name string).

Regenerated both packages.lock.json files: dotnet restore ArrTags.slnx --force-evaluate -p:RestoreEnablePackagePruning=false. The pruning-disabled restore reproduces the repository's existing lock-file convention and keeps the diff to the SkiaSharp additions (plus the test project's project-reference dependency list); the SDK 10.0.401 default pruning would otherwise have dropped unrelated framework-provided transitive entries.

The zip contains exactly: ArrTags.dll (864768 bytes), THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (1368 bytes), build.yaml (671 bytes), licenses/DejaVu-Fonts-License.txt (8816 bytes), licenses/SkiaSharp-LICENSE.txt (1129 bytes), and licenses/SkiaSharp-THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (139775 bytes).
Reviewed git diff: only the intended task-4.7 files changed; no unrelated production code was modified.
known_limitations: HarfBuzzSharp is intentionally not referenced; the task 4.8 spike decides whether it is needed (ADR-010).

Full native-asset and managed-dependency plugin-load-context packaging (copying SkiaSharp.dll, the Linux native asset, and a dependency manifest into the plugin zip so they resolve under the host's plugin load context) remains the Phase 5 packaging task; 4.7 only pins the packages and ships the notices, matching the scoped task text.

The PackagePlugin target copies the main assembly plus the notices/licenses; the SkiaSharp managed and native assets are not yet packaged, so the plugin cannot yet execute SkiaSharp at runtime. No renderer code consumes SkiaSharp in 4.7.

The lock files were regenerated with RestoreEnablePackagePruning disabled to match the repository's existing lock-file convention; the required ./build.sh restore (locked mode) passes with the committed lock files.
